brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at axial cells (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (2,0,0), joined in a straight row and locked with two joint bolts (jointBolt at (1,0) slot 3 and (2,0) slot 3). check_build: meshClash clear, no rule errors.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: Each cell holds a bin with stem hex-bin-full-drain (bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0, bin:2,0,0), the 'drained' full-depth tray. The stem name indicates drainage; I did not verify drain-hole geometry beyond the catalog name.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter use (herbs growing in the bins)
requirements.evidence: Each bin filled with soil and planted: basil-young at (0,0), mint-young at (1,0), thyme-young at (2,0). No PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL or prop warnings.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three full hex bases in a row, each with a full-depth drained bin, soil-filled and planted with basil, mint and thyme (young stage). Joint bolts lock the row. check_build reports meshClash clear and no errors; the only info note is open cap faces, which are optional. Drainage is taken from the bin's drained stem; material/waterproofing is not verified.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
